title: Conformance benchmark (expected failures and expected skips)
description: A benchmark file lists results the gate accepts. It uses the OpenID conformance suite's own expected-failures and expected-skips format, so run-test-plan.py --expected-failures-file and --expected-skips-file read the same file, plus four required fields that make every entry justified and traceable: comment, owner, spec and issue. run-test-plan.py ignores keys it does not know. One file holds one kind of entry: <component>.expected-failures.json or <component>.expected-skips.json.

owner.description: Who has to act to remove the entry: inji (a gap in Inji Certify or Inji Verify), suite (a problem in the conformance suite) or environment (a limit of the local test set-up, for example no public DNS).

variant.description: "*" matches every variant. An object matches when every listed key has the listed value; keys not listed match anything (run-test-plan.py, is_expected_for_this_test).

test_name.description: Test module name. Shell-style wildcards (fnmatch) are allowed, for example oid4vp-1final-verifier-invalid-*.

configuration_filename.description: fnmatch pattern matched against the path of the rendered suite configuration in the run folder. Use a wildcard such as *verify.oid4vp-1final-verifier*.json, because the folder differs between runs.

justification.description: The four fields every harness benchmark entry must carry.

comment.description: Why the result is expected, in one or two sentences. Printed in the report and in the TestNG known-issue message.

spec.description: The specification clause the result is about, as the suite names requirements (for example OID4VP-1FINAL-8.2), or a short clause reference.

issue.description: Where the gap is written up: a repository-relative path to an issue draft (docs/findings/...) or an https URL of a filed issue.

current-block.description: Block title the condition ran in, exactly as the suite log shows it; "" for no block, "*" for any block.

condition.description: Simple class name of the suite condition (the log entry's src), for example EnsureHttpStatusCodeIs4xx.

expected_skip.title: Expected skip
expected_skip.description: A module the suite is expected to skip (or, as run-test-plan.py also accepts, to fail) because the system under test does not offer the feature.
